context.story_title: User Can Manually Input Syllabus Topics
context.section_tech_spec_epic_3_relevance: This story primarily implements **AC3** from `tech-spec-epic-3.md`: "The user has an option to input topics manually if AI parsing is not desired or fails." This feature provides a crucial fallback mechanism for the AI Study Plan Generation workflow, ensuring that users can always create a plan regardless of AI service availability or accuracy. Manually entered topics will use the same data structure as AI-extracted topics, which will then be passed to the `POST /generate-schedule` endpoint.
context.section_architecture_relevance: As per `solution-architecture.md` and `tech-spec-epic-3.md`, the Next.js Frontend is responsible for capturing all user input related to plan generation. For manual topic input, the frontend will manage the topic data client-side. There is no direct backend API call for *submitting* manually entered topics; they are part of the larger payload for `POST /generate-schedule`.
context.section_ux_design_specification_relevanc: This story enhances **Step 2: "Add Syllabus"** and **Step 3: "Confirm Topics"** of the "Journey: Initial Study Plan Generation" wizard as described in the UX Design Specification (Section 5.1). - In Step 2, it provides the "Paste Topics Manually" option. - In Step 3, it requires the UI to handle manually added topics (editing, deleting) in the same way as AI-extracted topics. It should adhere to general UX patterns for "Form Patterns" and ensure "Clarity over Clutter".
context.ui_ux_considerations:
**Step 2: Add Syllabus** - Clearly present the choice between "Upload Syllabus" (AI parsing) and "Manually Add Topics". This could be a tabbed interface, radio buttons, or distinct sections. - If "Manually Add Topics" is selected: - Provide an "Add New Topic" button that dynamically adds a new input row/card for a topic title and description. - Each topic input should have inline edit/delete functionality. - Ensure clear visual separation and feedback.
**Step 3: Confirm Topics** - The UI in this step must be flexible enough to display and allow editing/deletion for both AI-extracted topics (from story-3-001) and manually added topics (from this story). The visual representation should be consistent regardless of the origin.
context.developer_notes: - **Frontend:** - Design the UI flow in Step 2 to allow users to choose between AI parsing and manual input. - Implement client-side state management for the `Topic[]` array, ensuring it can handle additions, edits, and deletions of individual topics. - Ensure that the client-side topic data structure matches the `Topic` interface expected by the backend `POST /generate-schedule` endpoint. - Consider the UX for switching between AI parsing and manual input: e.g., if a user switches from AI to manual, should existing AI-parsed topics be cleared, or offer to convert them? (Initially, clearing is simpler). - The `uuidv4` function is suggested for generating unique client-side IDs for topics to help with list rendering in React (e.g., `key` props) and state management before they are persisted in the database.
